meta.title: Rana Tadpole · dead controller, warm chips
meta.author: DEADBOARD
meta.description: A real, sold pocket controller for platform fighters (147 parts: RP2040, 20 mouse-switch buttons, USB-C). On USB the computer sees nothing, and the owner says it gets warm in the middle. Is the RP2040 dead? Bench supply: 5 V on AUX_USB_VBUS (USB VBUS (5 V)).
hints: With Solver: SPICE + PWR, compare the supply current with what an RP2040 board should draw (tens of mA). Then measure the logic rail 3vDiode (C9) and the RP2040's core rail +1V1 (C4).

A rail held near 0 V while its regulator works means a short on that rail. The warm chips are the ones feeding the short, not necessarily the culprit: with the power off, inject current into +1V1 and watch the thermal camera, or use freeze spray.
Replace the shorted part (the Inspector shows its value). The RP2040 itself is fine.
